name: 2 Tone Records
ownershipStory: Founded in Coventry in 1979 by Jerry Dammers of the Specials and financed by Chrysalis, which agreed to fund up to 15 singles a year and release at least 10, leaving the label its own choices. Its contracts let an act leave after a single release, and Madness and the Beat both did. The label stopped operating in 1986; the name survives as a reissue imprint.
hook: A Coventry band's own label, funded by a major, that made Black and white musicians playing together its whole identity.
blurb: Jerry Dammers of the Specials started 2 Tone Records in Coventry in 1979. A bigger company, Chrysalis, paid for the records but let 2 Tone choose what to release, and bands could leave after one single, which is why Madness's only 2 Tone record is their first. Its bands mixed Jamaican ska with punk, and most had Black and white members playing together on purpose. That, and the label's black-and-white graphics, were a deliberate political statement. Its short life, 1979 to 1986, follows the recession under Margaret Thatcher that its biggest hit, 'Ghost Town', described.
